- Overestimate prices after recent spikes or positive sentiment; model tends to overshoot upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment; model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Forecast tends to lag in early periods (e.g., 1–3 days) — adjust for recent sentiment shifts.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp moves, especially when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), reduce forecasted price by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment turns positive after a dip, model often overreacts — cap upward revisions at +3–5% of recent range.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals without confirming sentiment reversal (e.g., no “sentiment bounce” before price correction).
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates late-period price peaks — add 1–3% buffer for sentiment-driven rallies.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecasts with 3–5 day moving average.
